tasks.short: Agree e-commerce priorities with management and users, then translate them into website changes.

steps.what: Export sales, funnel and customer enquiry evidence for the strategy discussion.
Reconcile reporting periods and calculate journey drop-off and commercial baselines.
Discuss buying barriers and proposed journeys with users.
Combine research and commercial evidence into opportunities and explicit hypotheses.

loop.input: Aggregate metrics, minimised research notes and commercial goals.
loop.output: Opportunity brief separating observations, hypotheses and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Reference evidence for observations; verify numbers against the baseline and review interpretations.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported hypotheses remain explicitly untested.
loop.why_not_simpler: Qualitative barriers need interpretation across varied user accounts.

steps.what: Agree target journeys, commercial priorities and acceptable tradeoffs with management.
Translate agreed journeys into website requirements, acceptance criteria and success measures.

loop.input: Approved strategy decisions, technical constraints and requirement templates.
loop.output: Draft change brief with traceable acceptance criteria and measurement proposals.
loop.check: Map every requirement to an approved decision; designer verifies scope and measurable outcomes.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; conflicting requirements return to the strategy owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative strategy decisions do not fully specify interaction behaviour or acceptance criteria.

steps.what: Configure approved website changes and release them after acceptance checks.
Review early outcomes against the baseline and recommend the next adjustment.

tasks.design: Connect the {ECOMMERCE}, {CRM} and {BI} through the {DATA_PLATFORM} to produce consistent commercial baselines. Bounded loops draft evidence briefs and website requirements in {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; people conduct user conversations and agree strategy. Existing {CMS} and {ECOMMERCE} approval flows release supported configuration changes, then {BI} reports outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reporting definitions differed across teams, and strategy decisions were disconnected from implementation briefs. User research and management alignment required sustained personal involvement.
tasks.enabler_now: Small integrations can standardise evidence, while bounded drafting carries approved decisions into delivery artefacts. Existing publishing controls can connect acceptance to release.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial causality, conflicting incentives and understanding buying barriers remain difficult. Bespoke checkout logic or cross-system commerce changes need additional engineering.
tasks.human_edge: The designer earns trust, recognises what users cannot articulate and negotiates commercial choices without sacrificing usability.

ambition.what: An assisted product-selection journey for customers facing complex purchase choices.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less report reconciliation and more user research and outcome review. The designer can propose journey experiments with clear success measures; pricing, budget and release approval remain with existing owners.

reach.task: Prioritise product-discovery and checkout improvements.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, fulfilment constraints and purchase-funnel measurement.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a journey change caused an observed commercial improvement.
reach.learn: Experiment design, sampling bias and causal inference.

evidence.claim: Data reconciliation, reporting and controlled publishing can use deterministic integrations and configured workflows.
Interviews and negotiated commercial priorities retain substantial human work despite automated preparation.
The digest provides no documented case establishing automation gains for e-commerce strategy collaboration.

assumptions: The company operates an online sales journey and has usable aggregate commercial reporting.
The release step covers changes supported by existing templates and configuration.
Research participation has an appropriate GDPR basis, clear notices and suitable retention.
Access estimates include national employee consultation where staff research or monitoring changes require it.
The proposed assisted-selection service requires validation before investment.
unknowns: Whether sales, funnel and enquiry metrics use compatible definitions.
Whether existing publishing workflows support staging, approval and rollback.
Which proposed changes require custom development.
Whether customers need assisted product selection.
Who approves commercial experiments and public website releases.
research_questions: Which buying barriers combine strong user evidence with meaningful commercial impact?
Which outcome measures distinguish better purchasing decisions from short-term conversion changes?
new_work: Review generated briefs for unsupported conclusions and scope changes.
Maintain metric definitions and investigate incomplete exports.
Manage research consent, retention and participant recruitment.
Review release exceptions and interpret experiment outcomes.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with management or users to develop e-commerce strategies and to integrate these strategies with Web sites.

tasks.short: Coordinate with developers to agree, implement and accept website designs.

steps.what: Collect current designs, requirements, open issues and delivery status.
Discuss feasibility, dependencies and trade-offs with developers.
Document agreed states, behaviours, acceptance criteria and implementation details.

loop.input: Approved design decisions, linked design states and an acceptance-criteria template.
loop.output: Draft implementation specification with source links and explicit unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate required fields and links; designer checks behaviour, accessibility and unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per specification; unresolved details return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but prose decisions require interpretation into precise interaction criteria.

steps.what: Chase dependencies and reconcile delivery updates across messages and issue records.
Review the implemented interface and agree acceptance or further changes.

tasks.design: Connect design references in {DOCS} to work items in {PROJECT}, generating a live coordination pack and dependency alerts. A bounded drafting loop prepares specifications from agreed decisions; the designer approves them and retains feasibility discussions and design acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design references, implementation decisions and delivery updates live in different places. Agreement depends on conversation, while maintaining the supporting records takes separate effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing links, templates and notification rules handle much of the coordination. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, while bounded drafting handles informal decision notes.
tasks.still_hard: Changing priorities, undocumented constraints and design intent still require discussion. Design-file access and reliable version references may be expensive to integrate.
tasks.human_edge: The designer negotiates compromises and recognises when technically correct work weakens the intended experience.

ambition.what: Resolve interaction trade-offs at each prototype checkpoint instead of waiting for final implementation.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less status chasing and more early design review with developers. The designer can gain delegated authority to accept component-level interaction changes within an agreed scope.

reach.task: Translate campaign objectives into measurable website acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Campaign measurement, scope negotiation and the distinction between delivery and customer outcomes.

evidence.claim: Linked work records, templates and dependency notifications can replace repeated status assembly.
GitHub Copilot supports coding and review with oversight; this supports connector construction, not autonomous design acceptance.
Developer field trials report productivity gains, but do not establish a specific speedup for this coordination workflow.

assumptions: A typical team uses shared design documents, work records and chat; the shares are planning estimates.
The priors correctly suggest substantial human coordination, but record maintenance can change independently.
The solution tracks delivery items rather than individual employee productivity.
Estimates cover one team and one work-record integration; national consultation requirements may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether design decisions have stable links and identifiable owners.
Which interfaces and permissions are available for shared work records.
Who can approve design changes and accept implementation.
Whether national rules or existing agreements require employee consultation.
research_questions: Can source-linked specification drafts preserve interaction intent without creating extra developer clarification work?
new_work: Review generated specifications and resolve missing decisions.
Maintain document-to-work-item mappings and notification rules.
Investigate stale links and conflicting delivery updates.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with web development professionals, such as front-end or back-end developers, to complete the full scope of Web development projects.

tasks.short: Coordinate resolution of website infrastructure and hosting issues.

steps.what: Collect affected pages, error details, recent changes, and available monitoring evidence.
Write a support request explaining symptoms, business impact, and reproduction steps.

loop.input: Incident evidence, campaign schedule, and support-request template.
loop.output: Support request with evidence links and explicit unknowns.
loop.check: Validate required fields and evidence links; designer checks impact and removes sensitive data.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing evidence returns to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Symptoms and business impact arrive as free text and need concise explanation.

steps.what: Discuss diagnosis, responsibilities, and feasible remedies with operations or the hosting provider.
Approve the proposed change window, outage allowance, and rollback responsibility.
Check affected pages and critical journeys after the reported fix using browser testing tools.
Record resolution evidence and close the support ticket.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects release and monitoring evidence into the {HELPDESK}; a bounded model loop drafts the support request for review before sending. People handle diagnosis discussions and change approval, while deterministic journey checks attach results and configured rules close eligible tickets.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sat across hosting, release, and support records. Provider discussions and change ownership were difficult to standardise.
tasks.enabler_now: Small connectors and test harnesses are cheaper to build with coding assistance. Existing ticket rules can handle routing and closure once evidence is structured.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults, restricted hosting access, and disagreements about responsibility still need experienced people.
tasks.human_edge: Explain commercial impact, negotiate priorities, and recognise when a technically successful fix still harms visitors.

ambition.what: Campaign-launch website readiness checks.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time assembling evidence and chasing closure, with more time checking visitor impact. Infrastructure change authority stays with the operations lead; no new production rights are assumed.

reach.task: Assess campaign-launch readiness.
reach.learn: Translate failed website journeys into launch risks and fallback options.

evidence.claim: Evidence collection, fixed journey checks, and conditional ticket closure can use deterministic integration and configured workflows.
TOPdesk offers ticket summarisation and category suggestions, supporting assisted support preparation rather than autonomous resolution.
Playwright Test Agents can draft and repair tests; accepted tests can then run deterministically.

assumptions: The company uses a support queue, although hosting discussions may continue through the {EMAIL} or calls.
The OTHER category is website monitoring in s1 and browser testing tools in s5.
Operations implements the fix; implementation time is outside this coordination task.
Automatic closure applies only to predefined checks with no unresolved designer objection.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Logs are minimised; employee consultation follows national rules where monitoring affects staff.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for a limited pilot, including access and applicable consultation; customer waiting periods may extend elapsed time.
The estimates do not assume a 10-to-100-fold productivity gain.
unknowns: Which hosting evidence and release records are accessible.
Who can approve outages and provider changes.
Whether a formal support queue exists.
Whether the monitoring scope observes employees and triggers consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Which checks reliably distinguish recovery from a temporary successful response?
How much sensitive information can be removed without weakening diagnosis?
new_work: Review drafted support requests before sending.
Maintain evidence connectors and critical-journey checks.
Handle failed checks, stale release records, and premature closure exceptions.
tasks.statement: Communicate with network personnel or Web site hosting agencies to address hardware or software issues affecting Web sites.

tasks.short: Research user needs and turn feedback into design requirements.

steps.what: Define research questions, participant criteria and methods in {DOCS}.
Recruit participants, explain participation terms and arrange sessions through {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}.
Interview participants or observe usability sessions and record observations.
Combine research notes and existing feedback into an evidence pack in {DOCS}.
Group observations, inspect contradictions and describe themes in {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved evidence pack with stable observation identifiers and unnecessary personal details removed.
loop.output: Draft themes, supporting observation identifiers, contradictions and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Validate identifiers automatically; designer checks quotations, interpretation, minority experiences and unsupported generalisations.
loop.stop: One pass per bounded batch and one repair pass; unresolved or conflicting material goes to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules can count labels but cannot reliably interpret varied descriptions of user difficulties.

steps.what: Translate findings into prioritised design requirements in {PROJECT}.
Agree which requirements enter the delivery backlog.

tasks.design: Configure recruitment and scheduling through {WORKFLOW}, {EMAIL} and {CALENDAR}, then assemble approved evidence from {DOCS} and {HELPDESK}. A bounded loop drafts traceable themes; the designer conducts sessions and interprets findings, while agreed requirements enter {PROJECT} after the manager's decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scheduling and evidence assembly crossed separate records. Interpreting observations required context that fixed labels could not capture.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing scheduling features and small integrations handle coordination. Bounded text classification can prepare a traceable first synthesis.
tasks.still_hard: Recruiting a representative sample, observing behaviour and distinguishing stated preferences from actual needs remain demanding. GDPR requires a lawful basis, minimisation and suitable retention.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, ask useful follow-up questions and recognise when an apparent pattern reflects a biased sample.

ambition.what: Research participation for customers who use assistive technology.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into scheduling and assembling notes; more goes into observation and testing competing explanations. With agreed delegation, the designer can select follow-up studies within a research budget.

reach.task: Design participant sampling and distinguish segment differences from sampling noise.
reach.learn: Sampling methods, recruitment bias and the limits of qualitative evidence.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, evidence assembly and a bounded synthesis loop are feasible design patterns; research interpretation remains human.
Model-driven document metadata extraction exists, but outputs can be wrong; this supports reviewed extraction, not autonomous research conclusions.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results for this occupation.

assumptions: The company conducts project-based qualitative research and also receives customer feedback through the {HELPDESK}.
Existing participation records can govern permitted research use.
National rules may require employee consultation when staff participate or their behaviour is recorded.
The proposed use analyses design feedback without rating employees; EU AI Act obligations depend on the implemented use.
unknowns: Available recruitment channels, research budget and access needs of participants.
Lawful basis, recording permissions, retention periods and approved processing locations.
Whether national rules require works-council or employee consultation.
Whether the designer may commission follow-up studies.
research_questions: Can a pilot preserve contradictory observations and source traceability while reducing synthesis effort?
Which recruitment and scheduling features are already available in the {WORKFLOW} and {CALENDAR}?
new_work: Check theme drafts against observations and retain minority findings.
Review free-text evidence for unnecessary personal information before model processing.
Maintain evidence identifiers, access permissions and retention rules.
Resolve failed invitations, integration errors and participant withdrawal requests.
tasks.statement: Conduct user research to determine design requirements and analyze user feedback to improve design quality.

tasks.short: Agree priorities, resolve design conflicts and choose solutions with management and development teams.

steps.what: Collect requests and feedback from the {PROJECT}, {EMAIL} and {DOCS}.
Assemble options, estimates and supporting evidence in the {DOCS}.
Discuss user needs, delivery constraints and conflicting preferences.
Choose priorities, content criteria and an acceptable delivery scope.
Write the decision note and agreed actions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Typed discussion notes, explicit approved priorities and content criteria.
loop.output: A draft decision note with decisions, unresolved questions, owners and deadlines.
loop.check: Require source references. Flag missing owners and dates. Check decisions against explicit approval fields.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per meeting; unresolved conflicts return to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template handles headings, but discussion notes express agreements and qualifications in free text.

steps.what: Check the decision note and update owners, priorities and dates in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configured intake in the {PROJECT} captures requests and links evidence from the {DOCS} and {BI}; a deterministic generator assembles the option pack. People negotiate and approve priorities, then a bounded drafting loop prepares the decision note. The designer checks the proposed changes before the {WORKFLOW} updates the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests and evidence were scattered, while decisions depended on negotiation. Connecting records and maintaining meeting packs often cost more than the paperwork saved.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and connectors cover intake. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building the comparison pack, while a bounded model can draft notes from supplied evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Teams may disagree about value, capacity or authority. Software cannot settle those disputes or turn uncertain estimates into reliable commitments.
tasks.human_edge: Make competing interests explicit, recognise unstated concerns and negotiate a commitment people will honour.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on the highest-value customer journey obstacle to remove.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence gathering and minute writing, leaving more time for user evidence and negotiation. With explicit delegation, the designer can sequence small changes inside an approved scope; budget decisions remain with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Prioritise landing-page improvements against campaign objectives.
reach.learn: Campaign economics, capacity trade-offs and the limits of delegated spending authority.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, linked evidence and approval flows can automate coordination without automating negotiation.
Drafting a reliable decision note from supplied notes is plausible, but this digest contains no direct design-meeting case.

assumptions: This describes a marketing design team in a company with 200 to 2,000 staff; time shares are estimates.
The design review group includes relevant management, content and development roles.
Configured connectors can collect selected records and links without interpreting their meaning.
Typed notes are sufficient; recording meetings is unnecessary.
Build ranges are working effort. Access work includes privacy review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable; waiting time may extend delivery.
unknowns: Which request channels and connectors are available.
Who can approve scope, content criteria and priority changes.
Whether estimates and user evidence are recorded consistently.
Whether the proposed data processing requires employee consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Does structured intake reduce preparation time without excluding informal requests?
How often do draft notes misstate a decision, qualification or owner?
new_work: Check draft decision notes and proposed backlog changes.
Resolve incomplete requests and contradictory approvals.
Maintain intake fields, evidence links and access permissions.
tasks.statement: Confer with management or development teams to prioritize needs, resolve conflicts, develop content criteria, or choose solutions.

tasks.short: Create and maintain a searchable index of website content.

steps.what: Define searchable content, exclusions and useful search fields.
Inspect published pages and retrieve content from the {CMS}.
Map titles, body text, categories and exclusions in the {CMS}.
Build the searchable index in the {CMS}.
Test representative searches, missing pages and excluded content.
Activate the tested index for website visitors.

tasks.design: Configure the {CMS} to index approved public content after publication, using saved field mappings and exclusions. A deterministic check on the {DATA_PLATFORM} tests coverage and representative queries, with results in the {BI}; the website owner approves initial activation and material scope changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Content fields and exclusions differed between page types, while index maintenance lacked a clear owner. Existing indexing features may simply have been underconfigured.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing indexing features handle routine refreshes. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building missing connectors and repeatable checks; no model is needed at runtime.
tasks.still_hard: Search relevance, multilingual content, inaccessible source formats and distinguishing poor results from missing content still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: The designer understands visitor intent and decides which results help people complete their task.

ambition.what: Weekly prioritisation of content gaps revealed by unsuccessful searches.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time rebuilding indices and more time testing search journeys. With delegated authority, they can prioritise search configuration fixes within agreed publishing rules.

reach.task: Prioritise landing-page improvements using internal search demand.
reach.learn: Query intent analysis and the difference between internal search relevance and external search visibility.

evidence.claim: Configured indexing, field mappings and scheduled checks can handle standard public website content without a model.
GitHub Copilot supports code completion and review, which can assist implementation; this does not establish a build-time multiplier.
GDPR applies when search queries or logs contain personal data; employee monitoring may also trigger consultation under national rules.

assumptions: This task concerns internal website search over published public pages.
The {CMS} provides an indexer, configurable fields and a staging facility.
Routine refreshes use approved settings; material scope changes receive approval.
The configured {CMS} route is preferred despite the prior suggesting limited standard-software coverage.
Build ranges cover one website and existing hosting; they are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which indexing and staging capabilities the current {CMS} exposes.
Content volume, languages and non-page document formats.
Whether restricted content shares the publishing environment.
Who can approve activation and configuration changes.
Whether search logs identify visitors or employees and require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can publication events trigger incremental indexing using existing configuration?
Which representative queries and exclusion tests reliably detect regressions?
new_work: Review failed coverage checks and poor-result queries.
Maintain field mappings, exclusions and search test cases.
Check connectors after publishing schema changes.
Manage retention and access for any personal data in search logs.
tasks.statement: Create searchable indices for Web page content.

tasks.short: Create and test website prototypes covering interfaces, interactions, logic and representative data.

steps.what: Clarify the prototype's audience, target journey and questions to test.
Define entities, relationships, journey states and interaction rules.
Sketch layout alternatives in an {OTHER} visual design tool.

loop.input: Prototype brief, approved component catalogue, model and brand constraints.
loop.output: Structured layout alternatives using permitted components and explicit interaction states.
loop.check: Validate component references and required states; designer selects and edits the layout.
loop.stop: At most two alternatives and one correction pass; fall back to an approved layout pattern.
loop.why_not_simpler: Novel information hierarchy and spatial composition are not fully specified by reusable templates.

steps.what: Construct responsive screens and connect interactions in the {OTHER} prototyping environment.
Exercise sample data, screen sizes and interaction states using {OTHER} browser testing tools.
Observe users attempting representative tasks and discuss confusing interactions.
Resolve important findings and revise the prototype in the {OTHER} prototyping environment.
Package the prototype, interaction notes and unresolved questions for development.

tasks.design: A prototype generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines an approved component library with a designer-defined model and selected layout. A bounded loop proposes layouts; deterministic assembly, synthetic data and browser checks produce a private interactive prototype in an {OTHER} prototyping environment. User sessions remain human, while {DOCS} and {PROJECT} receive a generated handover from the reviewed prototype.
tasks.previous_blocker: Design tools made drawing efficient, but responsive behaviour, realistic states and handover still required repeated manual construction. Design assets and data models often lacked a shared structure.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes component renderers, schema-based sample data and browser checks cheaper to build. Bounded layout drafting helps where the brief leaves visual choices open.
tasks.still_hard: Original interaction design, ambiguous domain models and accessibility beyond automated checks need skilled judgment. A prototype cannot establish production security, scalability or integration correctness.
tasks.human_edge: The designer decides what to explore, notices user confusion and creates coherent interactions rather than merely plausible screens.

ambition.what: Include screen-reader users in early interactive prototype testing.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends more of the week exploring alternatives and observing users, with less repetitive screen assembly. They can choose which prototype hypotheses to test; production architecture and release decisions remain with existing owners.

reach.task: Turn brand direction into reusable interface components.
reach.learn: Responsive behaviour, design tokens and accessible component states.

reach.task: Specify interaction behaviour and error messages for implementation.
reach.learn: State modelling, concise interface language and task-based documentation.

evidence.claim: Component-based assembly, schema-derived sample data and generated handover documents are deterministic techniques.
Playwright Test Agents can draft test plans and tests and repair failing tests; generated tests still require validation.
GitHub Copilot provides code generation assistance that can help build prototype tooling.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slots denote visual design, modelling, prototyping and browser testing tools.
An approved component library exists or can be scoped to a small initial set.
Prototype data is synthetic and the prototype is privately shared.
Build estimates cover a reusable generator for one component family, not an entire design system.
Access estimates include participant consent arrangements and national employee consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Whether existing design components have usable code equivalents and export interfaces.
Which physical deployment, interface, logic and data models each project actually needs.
Whether the prototype environment supports meaningful assistive-technology testing.
Whether representative research participants can be recruited.
Which modelling and design changes require engineering review.
research_questions: Which repetitive prototype states can be generated without constraining useful design exploration?
Which usability questions require realistic data or working interactions to answer?
new_work: Review generated layouts and missing interaction states.
Maintain component mappings, synthetic data rules and browser checks.
Recruit research participants and manage consent and findings.
Keep prototype limitations and unresolved implementation questions visible.
tasks.statement: Create Web models or prototypes that include physical, interface, logical, or data models.

tasks.short: Design, assemble and maintain website pages, media and navigation.

steps.what: Review the brief, audience needs, content and website constraints.
Create layouts and navigation in a visual design editor.
Prepare approved copy, image crops, alternative text and page metadata.

loop.input: Approved copy, media assets, page context and editorial constraints.
loop.output: Draft alternative text and metadata alongside deterministic image derivatives.
loop.check: Validate lengths and asset references; designer checks meaning, image purpose and unsupported claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per asset; unresolved meaning returns to the content owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Image resizing is deterministic, but useful alternative text depends on the image's purpose in context.

steps.what: Assemble pages, navigation and reusable components in the website editor.
Review staged pages and test evidence, then decide whether to publish.
Publish approved pages and record the website revision.

tasks.design: Configure reusable page types, navigation rules and approval states in {CMS}, with approved assets supplied from {DOCS}. A deterministic asset pipeline handles crops and file checks, a bounded loop drafts contextual descriptions, and approved pages publish with revision records in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent components and scattered assets made each page a small custom project. Custom design decisions could not be reduced to templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable page schemas and asset rules remove repeated assembly work. AI-assisted coding can help build missing utilities, while editorial drafting stays bounded.
tasks.still_hard: Distinctive design, information architecture and accessible interaction require judgement. A weak component library makes initial setup expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a visual and interaction direction that fits the audience, message and brand.

ambition.what: An accessible campaign-page service for small internal campaign teams.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends more of the week shaping journeys and reviewing assembled pages. They can gain authority to accept routine page requests within agreed templates and capacity.

reach.task: Shape a page's message hierarchy before layout begins.
reach.learn: Content structure, plain language and editorial acceptance criteria.

reach.task: Translate search intent into landing-page requirements.
reach.learn: Intent mapping, crawlability and separating search assumptions from measured outcomes.

evidence.claim: Reusable content types, components and publication workflows can reduce repeated page assembly.
Coding assistants can help implement supporting utilities, with human oversight.

assumptions: The company maintains a public marketing website with staging and reusable components.
Editor and browser work dominate routine delivery; the supplied meeting share is too high for this task.
Custom component programming and full regression testing are counted in their separate tasks.
Build estimates cover a reusable starter, not a full website redesign, and overlap with supporting-code work.
GDPR applies to embedded forms and tracking; EU AI Act duties depend on deployed functionality. National rules determine any employee consultation.
unknowns: How complete the component library and content schemas are.
Who can approve content, branding and publication.
Which languages, accessibility requirements and audience groups the site must support.
Whether publication changes introduce tracking or employee observation.
research_questions: Which page patterns can preserve design quality through configuration alone?
How much editorial review do contextual alternative-text drafts require?
new_work: Maintain page schemas, asset rules and component examples.
Review generated descriptions and unusual image crops.
Handle requests that fall outside supported page patterns.
Monitor published pages for broken assets and content drift.
tasks.statement: Design, build, or maintain Web sites, using authoring or scripting languages, content creation tools, management tools, and digital media.

tasks.short: Develop, approve, and maintain website content style guidelines.

steps.what: Gather brand rules, existing guidance, and representative website content.
Resolve conflicting rules and decide voice, terminology, and accessibility conventions.
Draft content rules with examples for headings, links, forms, and interface messages.

loop.input: Versioned style sources, style decisions, and a fixed guide structure.
loop.output: Draft guide with rule identifiers, examples, source links, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require source or decision links; check coverage and contradictory examples; designer reviews meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved rules return to the editor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Voice guidance and useful examples require contextual writing beyond fixed document assembly.

steps.what: Review examples, resolve remaining questions, and approve the guide.
Publish the approved guide in the document store and link authoring guidance.
Email guide attachments to contributors for their local reference.

tasks.design: A deterministic collector versions approved sources from the {DOCS} and examples from the {CMS}; a bounded loop drafts guidance against recorded style decisions. Approval in the {DOCS} publishes a canonical guide and updates contextual links in the {CMS}, removing the need for emailed copies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules and examples were scattered, and documenting exceptions took substantial writing time. Teams distributed copies that quickly became stale.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned source extraction and document assembly are straightforward to build. Bounded drafting can turn explicit decisions into consistent explanations and examples.
tasks.still_hard: Brand voice, conflicting stakeholder preferences, multilingual meaning, and accessibility guidance cannot be reduced to formatting checks.
tasks.human_edge: Choose language that respects the audience and decide when a justified exception should change the guidance.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on recurring interface-copy exceptions.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time compiling and distributing guidance and more time resolving recurring content problems with editors. They can propose evidence-backed rule changes more often; approval remains with the editor.

reach.task: Resolve inconsistent terminology across website content.
reach.learn: Define editorial precedence and distinguish an intentional voice choice from an error.

reach.task: Adapt style guidance for another language.
reach.learn: Recognise rules that depend on language, culture, or local terminology.

evidence.claim: Source-linked drafting, deterministic document assembly, and approved-version publishing can reduce guideline production and distribution work.
SharePoint autofill columns supports prompt-based document metadata generation and warns of incorrect results; this supports cautious indexing, not automatic style approval.

assumptions: A typical company maintains guidance in the {DOCS}, with some teams still circulating attachments.
The editor can approve content conventions without a separate approval for every example.
Existing publication configuration can expose the approved guide from the {CMS}.
The high automation prior applies mainly to compilation and drafting; editorial decisions remain substantial.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Examples exclude unnecessary personal data; employee consultation follows national rules where applicable.
Build ranges cover one language and one guide, including access and applicable consultation. They are planning estimates.
unknowns: Which source takes precedence when existing rules conflict.
Who approves brand voice and terminology.
How many languages and content types need coverage.
Whether the {DOCS} and {CMS} support approved-version publication and contextual links.
research_questions: Can contributors apply generated examples consistently without additional explanation?
Which rules can be checked mechanically without producing excessive false alarms?
new_work: Review generated examples and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain source precedence, guide structure, and publication links.
Collect recurring exceptions for monthly editorial decisions.
Retire stale copies and check that contributors use the canonical guide.
tasks.statement: Develop and document style guidelines for Web site content.

tasks.short: Create visual interface concepts and revise them after stakeholder feedback.

steps.what: Review the brief, brand guidance, audience needs and existing interface patterns.
Create visual concepts using the {OTHER} interface design editor.

loop.input: Designer-selected direction, approved components, content and explicit layout constraints.
loop.output: Editable concept variants and preview pages.
loop.check: Validate component use, content completeness and responsive behaviour; designer judges hierarchy and brand fit.
loop.stop: At most three variants and one correction pass; designer continues manually if none is useful.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing components cover routine layouts; translating a new visual direction into an editable composition needs bounded drafting.

steps.what: Present concepts and discuss stakeholder reactions and competing preferences.
Revise concepts in the {OTHER} interface design editor.
Approve the visual direction for implementation or request further revision.

tasks.design: A reference pack in {DOCS} supplies approved content, components and constraints to a bounded concept generator on {DATA_PLATFORM}. tasks.short: Write and maintain interface manuals, testing protocols and design reports.

steps.what: Collect specifications, design files and test results from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
Choose the audience, document scope and required explanations.
Build document sections, screenshots, tables and test-result summaries in the {DOCS}.
Write instructions, explanations and limitations around the assembled evidence.

loop.input: Versioned source pack, audience, outline and document skeleton.
loop.output: A source-linked draft with instructions, explanations and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Check links, terminology and required sections automatically. Require sources for factual claims and flag unsupported instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per document; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can insert tables and headings, but audience-specific explanations require interpreting the supplied material.

steps.what: Verify technical statements and reproduce documented procedures.
Edit for audience clarity and approve the exact version for release.
Publish the approved version to the {DOCS} or {CMS} and record its location.

tasks.design: A generator assembles versioned specifications, approved screenshots and test results from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT} into standard document sections. A bounded model drafts explanations, followed by technical checking and editorial approval. The {WORKFLOW} publishes only the exact approved version to the {DOCS} or {CMS} and flags later source changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence changed across several files, and document templates could not write clear explanations. Manual copying also made documentation drift from the interface.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned exports and inexpensive generators can assemble factual sections. Bounded drafting can fill narrative sections while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented behaviour and weak source material remain expensive to resolve. Clear instructions still need someone to try the procedure and understand the audience.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what a reader will misunderstand and decide which limitations must be explained prominently.

ambition.what: Role-specific interface guidance for occasional regional content editors.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time copying evidence and more time checking comprehension with readers. They can propose audience-specific guidance, but publication authority changes only if explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Design task-based help for occasional interface users.
reach.learn: Information architecture, plain-language procedures and documentation usability testing.

evidence.claim: Structured specifications and test results can populate documentation templates deterministically.
Source-grounded narrative drafting with technical review is feasible; the digest provides no direct interface-documentation case.
GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance that could help build the generator; it does not establish documentation accuracy.

assumptions: The designer writes documentation, while a developer checks implementation details.
Approved screenshots and test results can be associated with a specific interface version.
Publication uses an immutable approved version; edits invalidate its release approval.
GDPR applies to personal data in examples and screenshots. Model access and EU AI Act obligations depend on the actual deployment.
Access effort includes any required consultation under national rules; elapsed approval waits are additional.
unknowns: Which documents are public and who holds publication authority.
Whether specifications and screenshots are versioned reliably.
Whether documentation contains personal data or confidential implementation details.
Which languages, accessibility formats and retention periods are required.
research_questions: Which sections can be generated entirely from authoritative structured sources?
Can occasional readers complete a task from the generated instructions without assistance?
new_work: Review unsupported claims and reproduce important instructions.
Maintain templates, terminology and source-to-document mappings.
Resolve stale-source alerts and regenerate affected sections.
Remove personal data from screenshots and examples before drafting.
tasks.statement: Write and edit technical documentation for digital interface products and designs, such as user manuals, testing protocols, and reports.

tasks.short: Write and review supporting website code, then merge tested changes.

steps.what: Read the change request and agree behaviour and acceptance criteria.
Inspect existing source, dependencies and component usage in a code editor.
Create standard component files, imports and configuration in a code editor.
Implement component behaviour, styling and focused tests in a code editor.

loop.input: Approved specification, selected source files, component conventions and permitted file paths.
loop.output: Isolated code patch and focused tests.
loop.check: Compile, lint, scan dependencies and run tests; designer checks behaviour and test independence.
loop.stop: At most two repair attempts within ten minutes; return the patch and failures to the designer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle scaffolding, but application-specific behaviour requires interpreting requirements and existing code.

steps.what: Run build, code-quality and focused test commands in a development environment.
Review the code diff, behaviour and check results in the source repository.
Merge approved code and update the change request.

tasks.design: Use deterministic templates and a bounded coding loop in the development toolchain represented by {OTHER}; keep each patch isolated with no production credentials. Configured checks validate the patch, a developer approves merging, and the integration updates {PROJECT} before website regression testing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting code varied by application, while reusable scaffolding and checks were often incomplete. Automating bespoke changes required too much custom logic.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistance can produce bounded patches against existing conventions. Deterministic generators and existing checks handle the repeatable parts.
tasks.still_hard: Unclear requirements, legacy dependencies and tests that confirm the wrong behaviour. Generated code still needs security and maintainability review.
tasks.human_edge: Defining correct behaviour and recognising changes that create hidden complexity or weaken accessibility.

ambition.what: A small-change component service for campaign teams.

tasks.altitude: The designer spends less time on scaffolding and more on interaction behaviour and code review. They can gain responsibility for accepting bounded component requests, while merge and release permissions remain separately assigned.

reach.task: Implement technical search requirements in reusable website components.
reach.learn: Rendering, structured metadata and performance measurement.

evidence.claim: Coding assistants provide completion and review capabilities, with oversight expected.
Field experiments found productivity improvements, but they do not establish this task's expected time saving.
A controlled study found experienced developers slower with the tools studied, so coding gains need local measurement.

assumptions: The designer writes client-side supporting code and has a development environment and source repository, represented by {OTHER}.
Code-editor work dominates; the supplied meeting and document shares are poor priors for daily implementation.
Estimates cover bounded component changes, not arbitrary application development.
Build ranges cover reusable tooling and overlap with website assembly and testing; they should not simply be added.
GDPR governs any personal data supplied as context. EU AI Act obligations apply as relevant; employee observation or evaluation requires separate assessment under national rules.
unknowns: Which languages, build tools and repository permissions are used.
Whether existing tests detect meaningful behavioural regressions.
Which source files and data may be supplied to a model.
Whether merge automatically triggers production publication.
research_questions: Which change types show a measured reduction in total implementation and review time?
Which checks catch defects that generated tests consistently miss?
new_work: Maintain templates, context selection and permitted file paths.
Review generated patches and the validity of generated tests.
Track rework and escaped defects alongside coding time.
Update toolchain dependencies and access controls.
